notes: CMEA's All-State page has been rolled forward to the 2027 (2026-27 season) audition and festival dates; the conductor/chair roster on that same page is still labeled 2026, so personnel were not captured. Audition repertoire comes from the CMEA HS Region & All-State Repertoire Lists 2025-2028 vocal document, whose most recent revision lists a 2026-2027 selection (the older PDF copy on cmea.org still says TBD for that year). CMEA runs two All-State choral ensembles: a Mixed Choir and a Treble Choir; the published audition materials do not differentiate requirements between them, and final ensemble placement is made by the festival committees.

organization.name: Connecticut Music Educators Association
organization.description: CMEA produces several auditions and concert festivals during the course of each school year, including regional festivals in four regions and a statewide All-State Music Festival. CMEA expects all students to participate in the audition process.

requirements.title: Audition components
requirements.description: Students selected for the All-State vocal audition prepare their part from a prescribed selection drawn from the coming year's All-State concert repertoire, performed in a Music Minus One (MM1) format. Four versions, each missing one voice part, are made available through the CMEA website and are the official MM1 for the audition.

requirements.title: Required scales
requirements.description: Scales are sung from memory using either solfeggio or a neutral syllable at M.M. quarter note = 92. Published starting pitches: Soprano G and D; Alto D and G; Bass D and G.

requirements.title: Sight-reading procedures
requirements.description: All-State sight-reading examples use two separate systems in two different keys (one for soprano/tenor, one for alto/bass), each written in both bass and treble clefs. Major keys only: sopranos and tenors in D, Eb, or F; altos and basses in Bb, C, or D. Examples always start on Do and may or may not end on Do, and may include notes from low Sol to high Re. Intervals may include thirds ascending and descending, all fourths, all fifths, and octave leaps. Examples are eight measures in 4/4 and may use half, quarter, and eighth notes and rests, dotted quarters and dotted halves. Students have 60 seconds to practice and are encouraged to sing aloud during that time. Singers may use solfege syllables, numbers, or a neutral syllable.

requirements.title: One voice part only
requirements.description: Students may audition in as many areas as they choose; however, vocal students may audition on one voice part only — Soprano, Alto, Tenor, or Bass.

requirements.title: Students with a disability
requirements.description: The child's music director must notify the Region Director of any modifications required for students with an IEP or 504 plan at least 30 days prior to the CMEA adjudication or festival. The school district funds any costs incurred by such modifications.
